writeup.headline: Arrowhead rates Hold at 47, just above Sell, as strong growth and cash offset losses and weak trend.
writeup.thesis: Arrowhead scores 47, a Hold, only 3 points above the Sell line. Growth (91) and the balance sheet (99) carry the score: TTM revenue growth of 16.9%, latest-quarter revenue growth of 171.0% year on year, and cash at 1.85 times debt, about 21.3 years of cash at the current burn. Quality is weak at 16, with an operating margin of -33.8%, a normalised FCF margin of -118.3% and diluted share count up 3.1% year on year. Valuation scores 13 because absolute levels are high, with a P/S of 12.7 and an FCF yield 14.3 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, even though P/S is cheaper than at 43 of the last 61 month-ends. The trend score of 31 reflects a price 32.8% below its 52-week high and shares 23.7 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days, while news (59) is mildly positive on analyst coverage and FDA progress for plozasiran.
key_risks: The company is still loss-making and burning cash, with a normalised FCF margin of -118.3%.
Revenue is lumpy and partly partner-driven. Sarepta can terminate on 30 days' notice.
The price is 15.1% below its 50-day average and 16.1% below its 200-day average, so the downtrend could continue.
Valuation is high in absolute terms at 12.7x sales, which leaves little room if the plozasiran sNDA or pipeline data disappoint.
Ongoing share dilution, with the diluted share count up 3.1% year on year and stock compensation at 10.5% of revenue.
what_would_change: A drop of 3 points would move the rating to Sell. Further price weakness hitting the trend score, or fading growth, could do it.
Reaching Buy needs 18 more points, which most likely means better quality scores from narrowing operating losses and cash burn.
A successful plozasiran sNDA filing and Priority Review outcome, backed by stronger sources, could lift the news score.
A trend recovery, with the price back above its 50- and 200-day averages, would add points.
